estrogen-hormone-skin-theories-dht-acne.summary: Forum ideas about managing acne by steering DHT, steroid and estrogen levels, built on the dermatology link between androgens, oil production and breakouts.

quick.overview:
These are hormone-based ideas for clearer skin. Forum posters link DHT, anabolic steroids and estrogen to acne and discuss anti-androgen or estrogen approaches as a way to calm breakouts and get a cleaner complexion.

The chain starts with androgens. Dermatology references describe testosterone, DHT and DHEA as raising sebum output, with DHT named as the main hormonal driver of sebum. More oil means clogged, inflamed pores and more acne. Steroid acne has been described mostly with corticosteroids in clinical settings such as transplant patients; the specific forum protocols have not been studied on their own.
quick.how: People usually discuss these ideas alongside ordinary acne care and decisions about hormone-affecting drugs. Anti-androgen and estrogen-based options are prescription medicines managed by clinicians, and any change in skin tends to be judged over weeks to months as oil production shifts.
quick.risks: Hormone-altering drugs carry medical risks that go well beyond skin, and anabolic steroids can themselves cause acne. Anti-androgen and estrogen treatments have their own side effects and are clinician-managed. Anyone with persistent or severe acne is usually directed to a dermatologist.

angle.text: The payoff is clearer skin: forum posters link DHT, steroids and estrogen to acne and discuss anti-androgen or estrogen approaches. The chain runs from androgens raising sebum output, to clogged and inflamed pores, to acne worsening or easing. Dermatology does tie androgens to sebum and acne, though the forum protocols themselves have no dedicated studies.

steroid-back-acne-management.summary: Keeping back and shoulder skin clear while on anabolic steroids or testosterone, using general acne care alongside a physique-building routine.

quick.overview:
Steroid back acne is acne on the back and shoulders that people attribute to anabolic steroid or testosterone use. People who train for physique want to keep that area clear so the back and shoulders look clean as well as built.

Androgen levels rise, sebum output increases, and breakouts appear on the oil-rich skin of the back. Wikipedia describes acne as a recognised effect of anabolic-androgenic steroids and testosterone replacement. Available reference material covers general acne and androgens; no trial dedicated to back acne from performance-enhancing steroids was found.
quick.how: People generally lean on standard acne care for the back: regular washing after training, clean fabrics against the skin, and over-the-counter or prescribed acne products. Forum discussion treats it as an ongoing side effect to manage rather than a one-time fix, and persistent cases are usually taken to a clinician.
quick.risks: Anabolic steroids carry broader legal and health risks beyond skin. Severe or scarring acne is usually managed by clinicians, and prescription acne drugs have their own side effects.

angle.text: The goal is a clear back and shoulders while building a physique. Rising androgen levels increase sebum output, and back and shoulder acne appears; acne is a recognised effect of anabolic steroids and testosterone. Management advice draws mostly on general acne information.

sliding-genioplasty.summary: Chin surgery that cuts and repositions your own chin bone to add projection, reduce or reshape the chin and balance your profile.

quick.overview:
Sliding genioplasty reshapes the chin by moving the bone itself. The surgeon cuts the lower part of the chin bone and slides it forward, backward, vertically or sideways, which changes chin projection and width for a stronger, more balanced profile.

Unlike an implant, it uses your own bone, fixed in the new position with plates and screws. It is used for cosmetic chin reshaping, facial feminization and as part of face-contouring and jaw surgery. Evidence consists mostly of case series and reviews, with few comparative trials.
quick.how: People usually have it done as a planned operation, sometimes alone and sometimes together with other jaw procedures. The result becomes visible as swelling settles. On forums it is discussed as a hardmaxxing option, often compared with chin implants.
quick.risks: Reported problems include swelling, temporary lip and chin numbness, infection, displacement of the bone segment and, more rarely, nerve damage. It does not correct the bite.

angle.text: A stronger, better-balanced chin and profile. The chin bone is cut and moved forward, back or sideways, changing projection or width in a way you can see once healing is done. Evidence is mostly case series with few comparative trials.

gonial-angle-reduction-v-line-surgery.summary: Jaw surgery that shaves bone at the jaw angle, sometimes with the chin, to narrow the lower face into a tapered V-line.

quick.overview:
V-line surgery narrows a wide lower face. Bone is removed from the gonial angle, the corner of the lower jaw, so the face tapers toward the chin. It is often paired with chin reshaping and is established in East Asian aesthetic surgery for patients with wide lower faces.

In looksmaxxing forums it sits at the opposite end from jaw implants: it removes width and angularity rather than adding it. Published evidence is mainly surgeon case descriptions and technique papers; a 1991 paper graded patients by the degree of angle protrusion and matched the resection to each type. No randomized trials were found.
quick.how: The operation is done through incisions inside the mouth under general anesthesia, followed by a recovery period with swelling. Some designs also take the outer cortex of the lower border and reshape the chin. Botulinum toxin in the masseter is a non-surgical option some papers describe for slimming the lower face.
quick.risks: Reported risks of mandibular contouring include nerve injury, bleeding, infection, asymmetry and unsatisfactory contour. Damage to the mental nerve is named as the greatest risk of jaw and chin reshaping in facial feminization literature. It is major elective surgery.

angle.text: A narrower lower face with a tapered, V-shaped jawline. Bone is shaved at the jaw angle, often with chin reshaping, and the change shows once swelling settles. It is established in East Asian aesthetic surgery, with evidence mostly from surgeon case series.

custom-peek-medpor-jaw-implants.summary: Patient-specific implants designed from a CT scan to add width, height or projection to the jaw angle and ramus for a more defined lower face.

quick.overview:
Custom jaw implants build a more defined jawline to your own measurements. A surgeon or design team models the implant on a 3D copy of your skull from a CT scan, and it is made in porous polyethylene (Medpor) or the rigid polymer PEEK and placed through the mouth. People use them to add width, height or projection at the jaw angle and ramus, often with chin and cheek implants.

The implant sits on the outside of the bone and adds volume. On forums, members share surgeon lists, post design files and compare planned millimeter dimensions, and custom implants are a common alternative to jaw-moving surgery. Published outcome data for purely cosmetic use is limited.
quick.how: People typically go through a design stage, planning target proportions with the surgeon before manufacture. The change becomes visible as swelling settles. Forum posters stress careful surgeon selection and design choices.
quick.risks: Risks of any facial implant include infection, displacement, asymmetry and nerve injury, and an implant can need removal. Forum posters note a wider jaw is not always more aesthetic and that some designs produce a rounder rather than more angular jaw.

angle.text: A wider, more defined jawline built to fit your skull. An implant designed from your CT scan adds width or length at the jaw angle and ramus, and the change is visible once swelling settles. Published outcome data for purely cosmetic use is limited.

ramus-vertical-ramus-augmentation.summary: Adding height along the vertical part of the lower jaw, usually with a custom implant, for a longer, squarer, more defined jaw angle.

quick.overview:
The ramus is the vertical branch of the lower jaw rising from the jaw angle toward the ear. Augmenting it adds height there, usually with an implant, so the jawline looks longer and more defined from the side.

It is discussed mainly as one part of a custom wrap-around jaw implant design. The published medical literature on ramus implants concerns dental anchorage and jaw reconstruction; no study of ramus augmentation for appearance was found.
quick.how: People generally approach it as a component of a custom implant plan made with a surgeon, rather than a standalone item. The shape change shows after healing.
quick.risks: Risks have not been studied for the cosmetic use. General implant risks include infection, displacement and nerve injury near the jaw.

angle.text: A longer, squarer jawline from added height along the vertical jaw. An implant placed along the ramus raises the jaw angle, and the shape change is visible after healing. Very little cosmetic outcome data has been published.

mandibular-advancement-surgery-bsso.summary: Orthognathic surgery that splits and moves the lower jaw forward to improve a recessed lower third, profile and bite.

quick.overview:
BSSO brings a recessed lower jaw forward. The surgeon splits the jawbone lengthwise on each side behind the teeth, slides the tooth-bearing part forward and fixes it with plates and screws. It is used for recessed lower jaws, bite problems and some airway conditions, and looksmaxxers discuss it for a stronger lower third and side profile.

It is a standard, extensively studied operation, usually planned with an orthodontist. Most research measures stability, nerve function and joint health rather than attractiveness. In forums it appears alongside genioplasty, Le Fort upper-jaw surgery and implants, sometimes as bimax surgery.
quick.how: People usually go through orthodontic treatment before and after surgery. Healing takes several weeks, with fuller bone remodeling over a few months, and a liquid-diet period follows the operation.
quick.risks: Documented risks include numbness of the lower lip and chin from nerve injury, relapse of the advancement, jaw-joint changes including condylar resorption, swelling and infection. Studies report neurosensory disturbance can persist in some patients. It is major jaw surgery.

angle.text: A stronger side profile and a lower third that sits further forward. The lower jaw is split and advanced, changing chin and jaw position and bite together. It is a well-studied orthognathic operation, though most studies measure function rather than looks.

facetite-renuvion.summary: Subdermal radiofrequency (FaceTite) and helium-plasma (Renuvion) treatments that heat tissue to tighten the jawline and neck without a facelift.

quick.overview:
These devices tighten loose skin along the jawline, jowls and neck without a facelift. FaceTite places a small probe under the skin that delivers bipolar radiofrequency energy; Renuvion uses helium plasma with radiofrequency energy to heat and contract subdermal tissue.

Heat contracts tissue and stimulates collagen remodeling, giving a tighter jaw-neck line. Surgeons describe them for patients with laxity too much for noninvasive devices but not enough to justify excisional surgery, sometimes combined with liposuction. Published evidence is mostly retrospective reviews and case series; no randomized trials were found.
quick.how: Energy is delivered through small access points, often combined with liposuction or fractional radiofrequency. Results develop over the weeks after treatment as tissue contracts.
quick.risks: Described complications include superficial burns, seromas, asymmetry and pigmentation changes, with rarer infection, nerve damage and scarring. The FDA has cleared Renuvion for specific indications and warned against off-label use. A 2026 paper discusses fibrosis and fat loss complicating later neck lift surgery.

angle.text: A tighter jawline and neck without a facelift. Heat applied under the skin makes tissue contract and remodel, tightening loose skin over the following weeks. Evidence is mostly case series, and the FDA has warned about off-label use.

morpheus8-rf-microneedling.summary: Radiofrequency microneedling that heats the deeper skin layers to tighten skin and remodel fat along the jawline and neck.

quick.overview:
Morpheus8 is a handheld InMode device combining microneedling with bipolar radiofrequency energy. It is used on the face and neck, including jawline and jowls, to tighten skin with less downtime than surgery for mild to moderate laxity.

Insulated needles deliver heat to the dermis and subdermal layers, which is described as triggering a healing response with new collagen, and deeper settings are said to coagulate a small amount of fat. Reviews and retrospective series report improvements; no randomized comparison against surgery was found.
quick.how: It is a clinic treatment, often done as a series of sessions and sometimes combined with FaceTite or liposuction. Skin changes build gradually as collagen remodels.
quick.risks: Described risks include burns, scarring, pigmentation changes and unintended fat loss. A 2026 surgical paper reports that fibrosis and fat loss after nonsurgical treatments can complicate later neck lift surgery.

angle.text: Tighter skin and a cleaner line along the jaw and neck. Radiofrequency heat delivered by microneedles remodels collagen and some fat in the deeper skin. The evidence comes mainly from case series and reviews.

hard-food-diet-tough-foods.summary: Chewing tough, fibrous foods to work the jaw muscles in the hope of a stronger-looking jaw and facial development.

quick.overview:
Followers eat raw vegetables, chewy meat and other tough foods to give the chewing muscles more work, hoping for a stronger-looking jaw and better facial development. It is also called tough-food chewing or ancestral chewing.

The idea is that chewing effort loads the masseter and related muscles. Reference sources describe the masseter enlarging with heavy habitual use such as clenching or constant gum chewing. No published human trial located has tested whether harder foods change adult jaw or facial appearance. It is discussed alongside mewing and jaw exercises.
quick.how: People work tougher, fibrous foods into everyday meals and chew them thoroughly, often alongside other jaw routines. Any change would be gradual, as with any muscle use.
quick.risks: Jaw-pain literature lists very hard foods among suggested parafunctional habits that may contribute to temporomandibular symptoms, though the link is debated.

angle.text: A stronger-looking jaw from chewing tough foods. The idea is that harder chewing loads the masseter and jaw so they adapt and develop. The chewing muscles do respond to heavy use, but no human trial has tested whether it changes jaw shape.

jaw-chewing-with-falim-gum-8-hours.summary: Chewing hard Turkish gum for hours a day to bulk up the masseter and widen the lower face.

quick.overview:
People chew very hard Turkish gum such as Falim for many hours a day, in some accounts up to eight, aiming for a bigger, wider masseter and a stronger-looking lower face.

Repetitive heavy chewing loads the masseter, which can enlarge with heavy use; clinical descriptions list constant gum chewing among causes of masseter hypertrophy, which can change facial shape. Forum users describe both enlargement they welcome and pain. No clinical trial of marathon chewing for appearance was located.
quick.how: Users chew in long daily sessions, often spread across the day, and compare progress by checking jaw width over weeks and months.
quick.risks: Reported effects include jaw pain, clicking or popping, pressure near the ear and more masseter bulk than intended. Temporomandibular literature lists gum chewing as a suggested contributor to jaw problems.

angle.text: A wider, stronger lower face from a bigger masseter. Hours of hard gum chewing load the muscle so it grows. Muscle enlargement from heavy chewing is documented, while appearance results from such long sessions are reported by users, who also report jaw pain.

chin-strap-while-sleeping.summary: A strap worn overnight to hold the mouth closed, used to encourage nasal breathing and a closed-mouth posture.

quick.overview:
A chin strap is a band that holds the mouth closed during sleep. Followers use it to encourage nasal breathing and a closed-mouth resting posture, often alongside mewing or mouth taping, with the hope of better jaw development.

It works mechanically by stopping the jaw dropping open while asleep. Reference sources note that chronic mouth breathing in children is associated with dental and facial changes such as a long, narrow face. No published trial located has tested chin straps for appearance.
quick.how: It is worn nightly as part of a routine with mewing, tongue posture work or mouth taping. Users generally describe it as a long-term habit rather than a quick change.
quick.risks: Mouth breathing usually reflects nasal congestion, and reference sources advise treating the cause. The health effects of related mouth taping are described as little researched.

angle.text: A closed-mouth, nasal-breathing posture that followers hope supports a better jaw and face. A strap keeps the mouth shut overnight. The link to facial reshaping is based on user reports; no trial has tested it for appearance.

myofunctional-therapy.summary: Tongue, lip and throat exercises used clinically for sleep apnea and tongue dysfunction, and discussed by looksmaxxers for tongue posture and jaw development.

quick.overview:
Orofacial myofunctional therapy is a set of exercises for the tongue, lips, cheeks and throat muscles. Clinics use it for obstructive sleep apnea, tongue dysfunction and open bite, and looksmaxxers discuss it alongside tongue posture and mewing in hopes of better jaw and facial development.

The exercises aim to change the tone and function of the oral and upper-airway muscles. A systematic review and meta-analysis examined it for obstructive sleep apnea in children and adults, and other studies look at its use with CPAP and in orthodontic cases. The evidence concerns airway and function; none located tests it for facial appearance.
quick.how: People follow a structured program of daily exercises, often guided by a therapist, over weeks to months. In looksmaxxing circles it is paired with tongue posture practice.
quick.risks: No notable risks are described in the sources consulted. Sleep apnea is a medical condition managed by clinicians.

angle.text: Better tongue posture and airway function that followers hope translates into jaw and facial change. Mouth and tongue exercises are used clinically for sleep apnea and tongue dysfunction. Studies measure airway outcomes; none has tested facial appearance.

jaw-contouring-makeup-contour-highlight.summary: Shading and highlighting along the jaw to make the jawline look sharper in photos, video and at events.

quick.overview:
Jaw contouring uses a darker shade to create shadow and a lighter shade to bring the edge forward, so the jawline looks more defined. It uses the same shading idea applied to cheekbones and noses.

The effect is optical: darker shades read as shadow and lighter shades as raised areas, changing perceived shape. It is visible as soon as it is blended and lasts until removed. The technique has a long theatrical and film history and went mainstream in the 2010s through celebrity and social media use.
quick.how: People blend a shade slightly darker than their skin under the jaw edge and a lighter shade along the edge, usually for photos, video or events, and remove it at the end of the day.
quick.risks: The sources consulted do not discuss risks; it is a temporary, cosmetic product application.

angle.text: A sharper-looking jawline on the spot. A darker shade creates shadow under the jaw and a highlight brings the edge forward. The effect shows as soon as it is blended and lasts until removed.

neck-tension-platysma-flex.summary: Tensing the neck muscle to sharpen the jaw-neck line in photos and mirror checks.

quick.overview:
Platysma flexing means deliberately tightening the thin muscle across the front of the neck so the area under the jaw looks more defined, usually for a photo or mirror check.

The platysma sits just under the skin of the neck; contracting it tightens and wrinkles the overlying skin and can pull the lower lip and mouth corners downward. The effect shows while the muscle is tensed. It is a posing habit, and no published studies have examined it.
quick.how: People tense the neck briefly while posing for a photo or checking the mirror, often combined with chin and head positioning. It is discussed as a posing technique, not a lasting change.
quick.risks: No specific harms have been documented. Clinical sources note that prominent platysmal bands can be aggravated by some activities such as weightlifting.

angle.text: A sharper jaw-neck line in photos. Contracting the platysma tightens the skin under the jaw, so the transition looks more defined while the muscle is tensed. It is a posing habit and has not been studied.

lower-face-rejuvenation-filler-jowl-fill.summary: Filler placed along the pre-jowl and marionette areas to smooth the lower face and restore the line of the jaw.

quick.overview:
Jowl filler uses injectable dermal filler, most often hyaluronic acid, to fill the hollow in front of the jowl and the marionette area so the jaw line looks smoother and more continuous.

The filler adds volume under the skin, and the result is visible right after injection. Hyaluronic acid products are usually cross-linked for stability. It is a mainstream aesthetic procedure, while trials focused on jowls are few and small; one registered trial of fillers for jowl improvement enrolled 16 participants.
quick.how: It is a clinic treatment done with injections in a short visit, with results seen immediately and settling over following days. Many people combine it with other lower-face treatments.
quick.risks: Bruising, redness and pain are common. Rare vascular complications can cause skin necrosis or permanent vision loss. Fillers are regulated as medical devices.

angle.text: A smoother lower face and a cleaner jaw line. Filler along the pre-jowl and marionette areas restores lost volume and softens jowls, with the result visible right after injection. Jowl-specific trial data is small.

jaw-expansion-via-mse-sarpe.summary: Surgical or mini-implant palate widening in adults, discussed in forums for facial width, cheek fullness and bite.

quick.overview:
SARPE and MSE widen the upper jaw in adults whose palatal suture has fused. In forums they are discussed for facial width, fuller cheeks and bite, often alongside braces or bimaxillary surgery.

An expander applies force across the midpalatal suture. In SARPE a surgeon first cuts the suture; MSE and MARPE anchor the expander with mini-implants for skeletal expansion, though many adult men may still need a surgical assist. They are established orthodontic treatments for maxillary transverse deficiency, and a literature review describes SARPE as gradually gaining popularity in adults.
quick.how: An orthodontist activates the expander over a period of weeks, followed by retention and usually braces. The process is part of a longer orthodontic plan.
quick.risks: Studies describe pain, some relapse, periodontal effects and other complications, with rare life-threatening haemorrhage reported. SARPE involves surgery.

angle.text: A wider upper jaw that broadens the midface and arch, with fuller cheeks and better bite. An expander widens the adult palate, after surgical release in SARPE or via mini-implants in MSE. These are established orthodontic procedures with documented complications.

braces-orthodontics-for-jaw-shape.summary: Established dental treatment that aligns teeth and bite and can change profile somewhat, especially combined with jaw surgery.

quick.overview:
Braces and other orthodontic appliances align teeth and bite, and in growing patients can guide jaws. People interested in appearance discuss them for a better profile and smile, often alongside jaw surgery.

Appliances apply sustained force to move teeth through bone, and palatal expanders and headgear can alter jaw alignment or airflow. Clinicians learned that perfect occlusion alone does not ensure good facial appearance. Severe jaw discrepancies may need surgery combined with orthodontics. Registered trials mostly address alignment speed, sleep and airway rather than facial attractiveness.
quick.how: Treatment is planned by an orthodontist and runs for months to years, with retainers afterward. For skeletal problems it is paired with jaw surgery before and after the operation.
quick.risks: Decalcification and decay with poor hygiene are described, and relapse is frequent, so retainers are often recommended. Facial-aesthetic outcomes are less studied than dental ones.

angle.text: A better bite, straighter teeth and a more balanced profile and smile. Appliances align teeth and guide jaw position, and combined with jaw surgery they can change the profile more. Studies focus on dental outcomes more than facial looks.

prf-prp-face-contouring.summary: Concentrates made from your own blood and injected or applied to the face for skin quality and volume.

quick.overview:
PRP and PRF are made by spinning a person's own blood to concentrate platelets and growth factors, then injecting or applying them to the face. People use them for fresher skin and some added volume.

Platelet-rich plasma has platelet levels typically 3 to 5 times normal and is believed to release growth factors that aid tissue repair. Aesthetic clinics use it for wrinkles and fine lines, often with microneedling in vampire facials. Wikipedia describes the evidence overall as mixed, and registered trials of platelet-rich fibrin focus mainly on dental and nerve applications.
quick.how: It is a clinic treatment: blood is drawn, processed and applied by injection or with microneedling, often as a series of sessions. Skin changes build over weeks.
quick.risks: Adverse effects are generally low, though improper equipment reuse caused a 2024 HIV cluster at an unlicensed spa. Preparation varies by clinic, so infection control matters.

angle.text: Fresher, fuller-looking skin from your own blood. Concentrated platelets and growth factors are injected or applied to the face to support tissue repair and skin quality. Clinics use them for skin, while true contouring has not been trialled.

tongue-pressing-against-roof-tongue-push.summary: A forceful mewing variant that presses the tongue to the roof of the mouth, aimed at a sharper jaw and face.

quick.overview:
Tongue push-ups are a variation on mewing in which the tongue is pressed firmly against the roof of the mouth, sometimes in timed holds, with the aim of reshaping the jaws and face.

The theory is that tongue pressure on the palate guides upper jaw growth or shape. Mewing itself is associated with the orthotropics practice of John Mew and his son Mike Mew, and the American Association of Orthodontists has stated there is no evidence mewing improves the jaw. No studies were found testing this specific exercise.
quick.how: People practice repeated holds, or press the tongue up during the day as part of a tongue posture routine, usually as a long-term habit.
quick.risks: No specific harms have been documented for the exercise. Mike Mew was struck from the UK dental register in 2024 after a misconduct hearing involving child patients.

angle.text: A sharper jaw and face from pressing the tongue to the palate. The theory is that tongue pressure guides jaw shape over time. Orthodontic bodies say mewing lacks evidence of jaw change, and this variant has not been studied.
